summary: A cast-iron tower on a stone pier in western Lake Erie, lit in 1885 to mark the Bar Point shoal at the mouth of the Detroit River.

lens.where: Michigan Maritime Museum, South Haven (the second fourth-order lens used here, per LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Offshore in Lake Erie, reachable only by boat; the archive records it as not open to the public; the Coast Guard retains maintenance access.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised (22 KB placeholder), so only the NPGallery metadata page was used. Keeper roster comes from USLHS (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); roster.py flags it as facts only, and the story names only Northrup, Oldrey and Scribner from it, plus Keondway/Dissett/DeRusha who are also named in the 1921 Bulletin. Disagreements: yacht fire date (Bulletin 22 Aug, LighthouseFriends 21 Aug); Buffalo length (AP 635 ft, LighthouseFriends 625 ft); auction price ($188,500 LighthouseFriends vs about $188,000 Lake Erie Living); Wikipedia says $78,000 total cost vs Heap/LighthouseFriends appropriations summing to $68,000 (Wikipedia not cited); Wikipedia says original lens is on loan to Michigan Maritime Museum, LighthouseFriends says the second lens is there. The LighthouseFriends-only items (E. Blake 1886, carpenter death, 1932 rescue, radiotelephone, siren 1905, lens changes, gauge board) are secondary and should be checked against Lighthouse Board and Bulletin volumes if available (the corpus holds Lighthouse Board reports only from 1891 on, and no 1885-1890 volumes). The 1932 rescue date and the 1921 keeper names rely on LighthouseFriends/Bulletin OCR (interleaved columns; names matched by reading across the column break). Lighthouse Board report volumes cover fiscal years ending 30 June; the Constitution incident is dated May 1892 by LighthouseFriends and 'last May' in the report for fiscal 1892. The AP date: report dated 13 Dec 1997 says 'Friday', taken as 12 Dec (not stated). Ownership since Jamieson's death (2023) not found. No newspaper hits in Chronicling America for 1884-1886. Roster 1960s Coast Guard names are given only as USLHS lists them.
